title.narrative: Community Climate Change Adaptation and Resilient Project

description.narrative:
The Catholic Diocese of Maralal covers three administrative districts of Samburu Central, Samburu East and Samburu North, a total of 21,000KM2. It serves a population of 223,947 people. The area covered is arid and has been adversely affected by recurrent droughts leading to increasing levels of drought losses. To reduce the impact of recurrent droughts on target communities over the coming years, the Diocese of Maralal plans to implement a second phase of Disaster Risk Reduction Project titled, 'Community Climate Change Adaptation and Resilient Initiative".
The proposed project is meant to address the main problem of the target communities' ability to predict, prepare for and mitigate the effects of the disasters. Due to the cyclical occurrences of drought related disasters, it has been difficult to realize long-term sustainable development in the target areas. This has been exacerbated by the fact that the community’s traditional ways of predicting, preparing for and mitigating the effects of disasters have been over ridden by modern methods as well as poor access to government services.
The Community Climate Change Adaptation and Resilient Project Goal is to enhance target communities' resilience to hazards in Samburu North and Samburu Central to predict, prepare for, mitigate and develop positive coping mechanisms to the effects of drought by 2014. The project has six closely interrelated outcomes including: improved community and partner capacity to effectively engage in DRR and climate change work; improved awareness on climate change and environmental protection; improved access to potable water for human, livestock and agricultural use; improved hygiene and sanitation for target communities; and improved accessibility of target communities through construction of rural access roads.
The proposed project will be implemented in two divisions of Lorroki and Baragoi and will target a total of 6,500 beneficiaries. In Lorroki the project will be implemented in Longewani, Amaiya, Logorate, Lolmolong and Malaso while in Baragoi the project will be implemented in Logetei and Ngilai.
